main_concerns.concern: The carrier_probe may be a synthetic/self-referential gate rather than a true probe of Codex CLI hook capability. If the CLI can emit 'carrier-probe-ok' without firing SessionStart/PreToolUse/etc., then the preflight could either falsely pass when hooks are later broken, or the current 'block' is merely documenting an environment gap rather than proving the boundary hardening works against a real hook-capable CLI. The risk of explaining documents/receipts as completion persists.

minimum_fixes.minimum_fix: Do not claim production readiness. Obtain or build a Codex CLI configuration/invocation that genuinely emits project-level hooks (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop), then re-run the carrier preflight end-to-end. Until then, keep the status as 'boundary scaffolding in place, full E2E blocked by missing hook carrier', and store the blocker in a machine-readable registry the patrol loop consumes.
